script.problem: A quote isn't the BSB's exact words.
It has 2 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.

terra.problem: Saying silver would have made her story easier assumes what a few coins could have done; the text does not say.
Calling the question a trick comments on the choice card itself.
The creditor is described as coming, not as being at the door.
It guesses why the individual baker chose tithe, which Papa Dorin has not been told.
The joke about being paid back in neighbors does not make sense and fails the joke logic test.
The passage does not say nobody is storing anything there.
Her reply is not an explicit refusal, and the text does not describe her tone as kind.
The explanation is flat and repeats that rain and fields are not mentioned without adding much personality.
The text does not say the Shunammite woman's family has no debt or that she considers having no son a need.
It asserts that she does not want to be handed hope she cannot hold. The text does not give her reason for responding, and that statement is not marked as a guess.
The father tells the servant to carry the boy to his mother; the text does not say he sends him straight home.
The passage does not say that no one sent for her. It only records her request and her reply to her husband.
Saying her distress mattered more to Elisha than manners adds a comparison and motivation the text does not give.
The text does not say she stays right at Elisha's feet after he tells Gehazi to leave her alone.
The claim that a prophet only knows what he is told goes beyond what Elisha says about this particular matter.
The explanation adds a reason for Elisha letting her speak that the text does not give.
The text says Elisha tells Gehazi to take the staff, not that it is handed to him.
Elisha's instruction concerns greetings and answering greetings; the explanation broadens it to no chatting at all.
The text does not say whether the woman rides ahead. It says she will not leave Elisha and that he follows her.
The boy does speak in the passage: he cries out about his head in verse 19.
